source_observations.locator: Frozen Kāśikā and the online Bālamanoramā at 5.2.30
source_observations.observation: Frozen Kāśikā has two neuter citations. Bālā gives the downward meaning. The live Kāśikā transcription spells the second example with b where the pinned field has v.
Three affixes name a bending of the nose. Application to a nose or person is by association.
Provides the feminine avaṭīṭā and the associated masculine bearer in separate clauses. This observation concerns the first formation only.
The same name restriction continues with ni. Names for the bend, person, and analogies of dense hair and cloth are distinguished.
Orders two replacements with their affixes, adds the third k branch, then distinguishes the eyes themselves and the person.

source_observations.locator: PG37 frozen English field, Vasu at 5.2.33
source_observations.observation: The archived k equation ends in cillaḥ. The following eye section legitimately uses that same surface. Exact bytes are pinned in project_dependencies.
Nibiḍo agrees with the singular fist. The person to whom it belongs is represented separately by a genitive.
Mallinātha glosses the grip as firm and explicitly gives a self-opening paraphrase for the third singular perfect of bhid. Compassion occasioned by remembrance motivates the opening.
Splitting of wood of itself illustrates an action located in the affected entity. The classical examples and Kālidāsa’s poem have different participants.
The edition separates the two members of cipiṭa-nāsaḥ with an editorial caret. The finished compound describes the person.
